After their arrest, Stephen's alleged girlfriend Monica Hardin was charged with one count of second-degree criminal facilitation of a burglary, one count of criminal facilitation of theft by unlawful taking, and one count of what is listed as an other felony state offense. The Kentucky Department of Corrections indicates she was sentenced to three years of probation, which is set to end in November of 2026. However, she also held a warrant in Ohio for charges including two counts of breaking and entering, one count of theft from a person in a protected class, and one count of grand theft auto. For her Ohio case, some charges were dismissed and others were reduced to a lesser charge, and she was ultimately convicted on, one count of misdemeanor theft, and one count of attempted grand theft auto. While it is not clear via Ohio's court website what she was sentenced, these charges carry a maximum consecutive sentence of 18 months in prison, meaning if she was sentenced to the maximum, she has already been released by the time this video is published. Stephen's charges and sentence were more clearly defined. He was charged with one count of murder of a police officer, two counts of possession of a handgun by a convicted felon, three counts of first-degree robbery, one count of first-degree wanton endangerment, one count of first-degree assault, and two counts of burglary. Many of his charges came with persistent felony offender sentence enhancements. According to the Kentucky Department of Corrections, Stephen was convicted on all counts and was sentenced to life without the possibility of parole, plus a combined 170 years. Few would like to donate to David, the surviving victim who was shot twice in the stomach by Stephen during the second carjacking. We've provided a go-fund me link in the description below. Thank you.

After their arrest, Stephen's alleged girlfriend Monica Hardin was charged with
one count of second-degree criminal facilitation of a burglary, one count of criminal
facilitation of theft by unlawful taking, and one count of what is listed as an other felony
The Kentucky Department of Corrections indicates she was sentenced to three years of probation,
which is set to end in November of 2026.
However, she also held a warrant in Ohio for charges including two counts of breaking and
entering, one count of theft from a person in a protected class, and one count of grand theft
auto. For her Ohio case, some charges were dismissed and others were reduced to a lesser
charge, and she was ultimately convicted on, one count of misdemeanor theft, and one count of attempted
grand theft auto. While it is not clear via Ohio's court website what she was sentenced,
these charges carry a maximum consecutive sentence of 18 months in prison, meaning if she was
sentenced to the maximum, she has already been released by the time this video is published.
Stephen's charges and sentence were more clearly defined. He was charged with one count of murder
of a police officer, two counts of possession of a handgun by a convicted felon, three counts of
first-degree robbery, one count of first-degree wanton endangerment, one count of first-degree
assault, and two counts of burglary. Many of his charges came with persistent felony offender
sentence enhancements. According to the Kentucky Department of Corrections, Stephen was convicted
on all counts and was sentenced to life without the possibility of parole, plus a combined
170 years. Few would like to donate to David, the surviving victim who was shot twice in the
stomach by Stephen during the second carjacking. We've provided a go-fund me link in the description below.
